exposomeSC

Study-aware, cell-type-resolved exposure association for population single-cell transcriptomes

What it does

exposomeSC tests donor-level exposures against gene expression within a cell type, for single-cell RNA-seq cohorts in which each donor contributes many cells. The exposure is a property of the donor, so cells from one donor are measurements of the same unit rather than independent replicates. The package therefore aggregates raw counts by donor and cell type and fits a robust edgeR quasi-likelihood model per cell type, with the donor as the unit of inference.

The case study the package was built around is smoking in the integrated Human Lung Cell Atlas, and a small part of those data is shipped with it. This README quotes no result; the tables and figures of the vignettes are computed from the shipped data when they are built.

Installation 

# From Bioconductor. Until Bioconductor 3.25 is released, exposomeSC is
# only in the development version, which needs R-devel:
if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("exposomeSC")

# Development version from GitHub:
BiocManager::install("CuiweiG/exposomeSC")

A first analysis

The package ships a small real data set: 352 tracheal epithelial cells from 12 donors of the Human Lung Cell Atlas, six heavy smokers and six never smokers, with up to 10 basal, secretory and multiciliated-lineage cells per donor. ?hlca_airway_subset gives its source, licence and selection rule. The data set shows how the functions are called on real counts; with 12 donors and at most 10 cells per donor and cell type it is far too small to support conclusions about smoking. A second real data set, ?incov_pbmc_subset, holds blood cells of 43 patients with their surface proteins, plasma metabolites and plasma levels of exogenous compounds, for the functions that need those.

library(exposomeSC)

scee <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "hlca_airway_subset.rds",
    package = "exposomeSC"))
scee

fit <- run_sc_exwas(scee,
    exposure = "smoking",
    covariates = "chemistry_v3")

head(fit[order(fit$pvalue),
         c("gene", "celltype", "log2FC", "statistic", "pvalue", "padj_global")])

The object was made by build_scee(), which checks that every donor in the cells has a row in the exposure matrix and that every row belongs to a donor with cells; the script that made the file checks that its counts are non-negative whole numbers. run_sc_exwas() returns one row per gene and cell type, with padj_global adjusted across the whole gene-by-cell-type family.

For the default edgeR backend, se is NA by design: the quasi-likelihood F test supplies no coefficient standard error, and statistic is the signed square root of that F statistic, a ranking quantity rather than a Wald statistic.

What the estimate is

The primary estimand is the adjusted association between a donor-level exposure and relative expression within a cell type. The workflow:

  1. takes raw counts and the donor of each cell from a container that has checked the donors against the exposure table;
  2. aggregates the sparse matrix by donor and cell type;
  3. retains the complete target-cell-type transcriptome library size;
  4. fixes expression support without inspecting exposure labels;
  5. applies TMM normalisation and robust edgeR quasi-likelihood inference;
  6. checks group support, design rank and numerical estimability; and
  7. adjusts across the full feature-by-cell-type hypothesis family.

The functions sum the counts as they are given and do not check that they are raw: counts that were normalised or corrected beforehand are summed like any others, and the models are then not the ones described here.

Cell-type composition is a separate relative-composition outcome. It is not an offset for the primary expression estimand, and captured cell proportions are not absolute tissue abundance.

Functions

Group Functions
Container build_scee(), as_scee() (from a rexposome ExposomeSet), seurat_to_exposure(), exposure_impute_lod(); accessors exposureData(), exposureInfo(), exposureVariables(), sampleColumn(), cellSampleMap()
Primary analysis run_sc_exwas() (edgeR, DESeq2 or voom-dream backends), donor_pseudobulk(), run_sc_exwas_pb_offset(), run_multi_exwas(), run_sc_exwas_glmm(), run_meta_exwas()
Design estimate_power()
Exposure modelling run_dose_response(), run_dose_response_gam(), run_interaction_test(), run_mixture_qgcomp(), run_sc_mixture()
Composition run_exposure_composition()
Downstream run_gsea(), run_cell_coupling()
Cross-omic networks (exploratory) simulate_crossomic_network(), run_celltype_network(), run_exposure_network(), run_comparative_network() and their plots

The network functions fit sparse Gaussian graphical models with the graphical lasso and the collaborative graphical lasso. An edge is a summary under that model for the donors analysed, not a tested conditional independence, and run_comparative_network() describes the differences between networks without testing them. The package estimates associations; it does not supply causal identification.

HLCA data provenance

The airway data come from the integrated HLCA collection of Sikkema et al. (2023), distributed under CC BY 4.0 through CZ CELLxGENE.

Item Pinned source
Publication Sikkema et al., Nature Medicine (2023)
CELLxGENE collection Integrated Human Lung Cell Atlas
Exact H5AD asset 688185ad-11c2-4172-a53a-f4f1f4076860.h5ad
Count layer /raw/X; /X is not used for count modelling
H5AD SHA-256 1cbdde1e513a31bdb6a3f70296e2d0612760d2af4032e239c94596ea87b44007

The example data set shipped with the package, inst/extdata/hlca_airway_subset.rds, is taken from this file: 352 cells of 12 donors of its study Seibold_2020, which is Goldfarbmuren et al., Nature Communications (2020). inst/scripts/make_hlca_airway_subset.R checks the size and the SHA-256 of the H5AD and makes the subset from it; cells and genes are selected and the counts are unchanged. The subset is redistributed under the same CC BY 4.0 licence.

The scripts that prepare the full ever- versus never-smoking analysis object are installed with the package, in the directory that system.file("scripts", package = "exposomeSC") returns. fetch_hlca.R rejects a missing raw layer, a changed asset size, and non-finite, negative or non-integer values. Each script takes the paths of its inputs and of its output as arguments; create_hlca_input_manifest.R takes first the directory, here ., in which it writes hlca_input_manifest.rds and hlca_input_manifest.csv. With the pinned H5AD downloaded as hlca_core.h5ad:

scripts=$(Rscript -e 'cat(system.file("scripts", package = "exposomeSC"))')
Rscript "$scripts/fetch_hlca.R" hlca_core.h5ad hlca_smoking_scee.rds
Rscript "$scripts/extract_hlca_design_metadata.R" hlca_core.h5ad \
    hlca_design_metadata.rds
Rscript "$scripts/extract_hlca_feature_metadata.R" hlca_core.h5ad \
    hlca_feature_metadata.rds
Rscript "$scripts/create_hlca_input_manifest.R" . hlca_core.h5ad \
    hlca_smoking_scee.rds hlca_design_metadata.rds hlca_feature_metadata.rds

The scripts need rhdf5, zellkonverter, AnnotationDbi, org.Hs.eg.db and digest, which the package itself does not depend on.

INCOV data provenance

The second data set, inst/extdata/incov_pbmc_subset.rds, is taken from the INCOV cohort of Su et al., Cell (2020): 1,032 blood mononuclear cells of 43 patients with COVID-19 at their first blood draw, with the counts of 192 antibodies for the same cells (four of them isotype controls), 182 plasma metabolites and the plasma levels of 13 compounds of exogenous origin.

Item Source
Clinical records, plasma metabolites Table S1 of Mendeley Data, doi:10.17632/tzydswhhb5.5, version 5, CC BY 4.0
Single-cell genes and surface proteins ArrayExpress E-MTAB-9357, redistributed under CC BY 4.0 with the permission of the authors who deposited it

inst/scripts/make_incov_pbmc_subset.R checks the size and the SHA-256 of the 88 input files, recovers the counts from the logarithms that the archive holds, assigns monocytes and T cells by gates on surface proteins and marker genes, and draws the cells; ?incov_pbmc_subset describes each step. It takes the folder with the input files and the output file as arguments and needs data.table and R.utils.

Documentation

  • exposomeSC: the container, the association model and the further analyses, each run on one of the two real data sets of the package
  • Network tutorial: exploratory cross-omic networks of two cell types and plasma metabolites, and their descriptive comparison, run on the INCOV data
  • Permutation and power: checks of a result on the airway data, by permuting the exposure among the donors and by a second backend, the two adjustments of the p-values, and a power approximation

On every push to main, GitHub Actions run R CMD check on Linux, macOS and Windows, BiocCheck, the test coverage and a check of the citation, the links and the spelling; the workflows are in .github/workflows.

Licence and citation

The code and the documentation of the package are under Artistic-2.0. The two data files in inst/extdata are not: they are parts of the data of others and are redistributed under CC BY 4.0. hlca_airway_subset.rds keeps the licence of the atlas. In incov_pbmc_subset.rds the clinical records and plasma measurements are under CC BY 4.0 as published on Mendeley Data, and for the single-cell counts, from ArrayExpress E-MTAB-9357, the authors who deposited them gave this permission on 21 November 2026:

The single-cell values from E-MTAB-9357 included in exposomeSC may be used and redistributed under CC BY 4.0, with citation of Su et al. (2020).

The two provenance sections above and the help pages of the data sets name the sources and the publications to cite.

To cite the package, use citation("exposomeSC"): it gives the Bioconductor DOI, 10.18129/B9.bioc.exposomeSC, and the version installed. When you use the shipped data sets, please cite their primary publications as well.
